what: Operator-level kernels at DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's real shapes. Unlike the playground corpus these are not teaching sizes, and they stress the part's bounds hard enough that most of them are refused as written -- which is the useful part.

shapes.source: The deepseek41 GGUF's own configuration. Every value below is read from it rather than chosen; a shape set with no cited source does not belong in this bench (see bench/shapes/registry.json).
shapes.ATTN_S_source: 8 positions: the engine's own `ds4_attn_sink_batched` block size (bench/engine/tile/attn_sink_1head_1blk.tile), and the extent the sink reference is parameterised at. The sink is a virtual position -- attn_dispatch.rs:1428-1490.

representations.tile: tile-dialect MLIR, generated from the shape table above.
representations.pto: PTO assembly from the in-tree rspto. Reproducible; a test asserts it byte for byte.
representations.ascendc: AscendC C++ from the in-tree pto-to-ascendc, for --soc 910b. Covers strictly LESS than the PTO column here, which is a measured fact about the two emitters rather than a gap in the corpus.
representations.tile-rs: Lifted from the PTO by ptoas-rs. Sparsest column: the lift models fewer ops than either emitter. COMPILED, and checked both ways -- every file builds against the kernel-side DSL, and the lift is checked to still accept the .pto each one came from, so a file cannot outlive the generator that produced it.
representations.searched: For a kernel the PTO emitter refuses, the tiling tile-search chose instead. Present only where a search succeeded.

a_refusal_is_a_result: Six distinct bounds are hit across this corpus -- a row-major tile bound, the unified-buffer budget, a blocked-matmul N multiple, an operand-load form, an mxfp4 pair-count multiple, and a fractal stride. Each is recorded per representation, because the two emitters check different things and disagree about several of these kernels. Of the kernels the PTO emitter refuses, tile-search finds an accepted tiling for most; the ones it cannot are the ones whose bound is not a tile extent at all, and that distinction is the single most useful thing this corpus says.

A row here claims `this kernel was observed correct on device`; a campaign `verified` record additionally claims `these exact bytes were, at the campaign's own tolerance`. The 2026-11-08 sweep is what made the second claim checkable: 13 artefacts across the tree did not derive from their own .tile, and until model_corpora_ascendc_matches_its_emitter.rs landed, only bench/playground16 was gated.

Reduce the number of buffers or the element count. This body accumulates across the width -- a reduction, a matmul or a matvec -- so the chunked path is NOT the repair: a chunk boundary would change the answer. gemm_f16_lmhead_v41_16x5120x12928.ascendc_refusal_reinstated_2026_11_08: REINSTATED 2026-11-08 (iteration 34), and the 2026-11-08 retraction above was WRONG. The retracted text named 'buffer 0 needs 81920 elements (163840 bytes)'. Those are exactly the numbers the artefact still had: pipe.InitBuffer(tbuf0, 51712) against a DataCopy(buf0, gm0Tensor, 16*5120) of 163840 bytes. The refusal was correct and the emitter had merely stopped DETECTING it. ROOT CAUSE, one token: mlir_to_cpp stands its chunker down for a body that accumulates across the width, via a case-sensitive substring search over the emitted text for ["ReduceMax", "ReduceSum", "tile_matmul", "argmax", "tile_matvec"] -- and the matmul arm writes the marker TILE_DEGENERATE_MATMUL, so `tile_matmul` matched NOTHING. Measured: 0 of the corpus's artefacts contain the string `tile_matmul`, while 5 contain TILE_DEGENERATE_MATMUL. With the chunker wrongly engaged, the body chunked its flat element count (66191360 as 2560 x 25856) while the matmul arm kept indexing the unchunked extents, and the capacity check passed because it sized the CHUNK (3 x 51712 = 155136 < 194560). The device verdict was 507035 at aclrtSynchronizeStream. The needle now matches what the arm emits, the body is offered to the capacity check unchunked, and that check refuses it with its own computed bound -- the message in ascendc_refused below, taken from the tool.
gemm_f16_lmhead_v41_16x5120x12928.ascendc_refusal_retracted_2026_11_08_WRO: This row recorded ascendc_refused = "UB overflow in kernel 'bm_gemm_f16_16_5120_12928': buffer 0 needs 81920 elements (163840 bytes) but only 62784 bytes available per buffer (188416 UB / 3 slots)...." and the emitter ACCEPTS this kernel: `pto-to-ascendc <its .tile>` exits 0 and writes the artefact now recorded above. The refusal claim was stale -- a UB bound that the buffer reuse and chunked-emission work stopped hitting -- and nothing re-ran it, because the only AscendC byte-identity gate pointed at bench/playground16. A stale REFUSAL is the same defect class as a stale artefact in the opposite direction: it understates the emitter and makes the corpus's refusal spread wrong.
gemm_f16_lmhead_v41_16x5120x12928.device_attempt_2026_11_08: FAIL aclrtSynchronizeStream(stream) -> 507035, 14s, run 2026-11-08 against device bytes hash-gated to cff9f65919537744 (= the repo's). CHUNK-BLIND MATMUL. The `// chunked:` window makes __n = 25856 elements resident; the TILE_DEGENERATE_MATMUL arm indexes the UNCHUNKED logical extents __mm_m=16, __mm_k=5120, __mm_n=12928. Out of bounds by its own constants: pipe.InitBuffer(tbuf0, 51712) against a DataCopy(buf0, gm0Tensor, 16*5120) of 163840 bytes, and buf1.GetValue(__p*12928+__j) reaching element 66191359 of a 25856-element buffer. The UB capacity gate passes because it is computed from the CHUNK WIDTH (3 x 51712 = 155136 < 194560 UB_ADDRESSABLE_TOP), so nothing refused it. AND THIS CORRECTS THE ROW ABOVE: the refusal iteration 30 retracted as stale said "buffer 0 needs 81920 elements (163840 bytes) but only 62784 bytes available per buffer" -- the SAME 81920 elements and the SAME 163840 bytes measured here. That refusal was CORRECT. What changed was not the kernel but the gate: chunked emission made the capacity check read a chunk width instead of the arm's own indexing, so the emitter stopped DETECTING the overflow rather than stopping committing it, and `pto-to-ascendc` exiting 0 was read as evidence the bound was gone. Degenerate is not the defect -- three other corpus artefacts carry TILE_DEGENERATE_MATMUL with no chunking and engine/attn_sink_engine_64heads is banked and passing. The composition is.

reshaped.pto_refused: blocked matmul: M=1 must be a multiple of 16 (910B2 cube fixedRowSize). Pad the M dim.
reshaped.why: the capture passes 6 operands where the i8 dequant matmul declares 7, dropping `scale: *const f32`. At 6 the blocked-matmul pre-pass cannot read the shape, so the emitter blamed one of our own passes (`detect_blocked_matmul_loads must mark i8 matmul inputs`). With the call corrected the true constraint appears and it is the part's: on the 910B2 cube M must be a multiple of 16, so this decode shape needs the padded M=16 form the corpus already carries.

gemm_i8_v41_1x5120x2304.pto_refused_rediagnosed_2026_11_09: WAS: matmul_i8: both operand loads must be deferred for blocked emit (a.deferred=false, b.deferred=false); detect_blocked_matmul_loads must mark i8 matmul inputs -- a MISDIAGNOSIS. The .tile call carries six args to the seven-arg dequant form, so `%m` was read as the scale pointer, `%k` as M, `%n` as K and N became 0; detect_blocked_matmul_loads requires seven args too and had correctly skipped the line. The emitter now checks arity before any positional read, and the refusal names the call.

mx4pk_v41_5120x2304.pto_refused_retracted_2026_11_09: RETRACTED 2026-11-09: the bound was a KNOB DEFAULT read as a divisor, not a capability. TILE_MXFP4_PAIRS_PER_CHUNK caps the chunk at 64 and the code took min(np_total, cap) and then refused when that did not divide the pair count. 80 pairs is not a multiple of 64 and never will be. mlir_to_pto now takes the largest chunk at or below the cap that divides the pair count and is a multiple of 8 (npc * 4 must be a multiple of 32 for the row_major none_box partials tile), which is 40 here: two chunks of 40 pairs, and ptoas 0.68 accepts it at rc=0. Kept rather than deleted so the refusal that licensed `pto: null` records its retirement. Was: mul_mv_id_mxfp4_pk: pair count (80) must be a multiple of the 64 chunk
mx4pk_v41_5120x2304.tile_rs_refused: refused bench/deepseek_v41/pto/mx4pk_v41_5120x2304.pto: `pto.get_block_idx` for `%pto24` is not lifted. `tile_std::get_block_idx` does exist, at the `tile_std` crate root -- but importing it would not help: `mlir_to_pto` deletes any line containing `get_block_idx`, and the grid-stride `scf.for` around this op is synthesised by that emitter from the kernel's shape rather than read from its input. This file is the expansion of one whole-kernel `__tile_*` call, and that call does not determine it: the tiling comes from an emit-time environment knob, so several corpus artifacts are the SAME call at different geometries and would all lift to the same Rust
mx4pk_v41_5120x2304.tile_rs_refused_repointed_2026_11_09: Was "no PTO to lift", which was DERIVED from this kernel's PTO refusal -- retracted the same day when the chunk cap was fixed. A derived refusal outliving its cause points at nothing. The real blocker is structural and documented at length in ptoas_rs: mlir_to_pto deletes any line containing get_block_idx, the grid-stride scf.for around it is synthesised by that emitter from the kernel's shape rather than read from its input, and this artefact is the knob-driven expansion of one whole-kernel call -- so lifting it to that call would emit identical Rust for files that differ. Kept out of the refusal text itself because every refusal is classified into exactly one kind and a quotation of the old one made this match two.

rmsnorm_v41_8x1280_quarter.device_check_resized_2026_11_08: THE EARLIER RECORD WAS UNDER-SIZED AND IS SUPERSEDED, NOT RETRACTED. It read: PASS 2026-11-07 on 910B2 (CANN 8.5.2 aarch64, dav-2201): elements=1280 wrong=0 max_abs=1.077e-06 max_rel=6.506e-07 against an f64 oracle. ORACLE 1, x/rms(x). The same norm tiled 8 rows x 1280 -- the quarter-width blocking. -- taken at n=1280 while the kernel touches 8x1280 = 10240 floats. main.asc allocates n*sizeof(float) per pointer and the oracles compare n elements, so that run filled one row, compared one row, and let the kernel write seven more rows past a 5120-byte allocation. Three runs settle it. (1) n=1280, default input: wrong=0 max_rel=6.506e-07 -- reproduces the banked figure to the digit. (2) n=10240, default input: wrong=10240 max_rel=7.058e+00. (3) n=10240, ROW-PERIODIC input: wrong=0 max_rel=2.933e-08. Run 2 is NOT evidence the kernel is wrong -- ORACLE 1's denominator is one global rms and the kernel's is one per row, so at n=10240 on arbitrary input the oracle asks for a different function and every element must disagree, row 0 included. Run 3 removes that confound by making the two denominators equal, and the kernel passes on all 10240 elements. So the artefact was right and the EVIDENCE was the defect.

rope_v41_8x64.rope_pos0_is_exact_2026_11_09: SUPERSEDES the 2026-11-08 ineligibility note below, which is kept with its date because the direction of travel is the information. The tile declares `%p = llvm.mlir.constant(0 : i32)`: rope rotates each pair by theta = pos * freq, so at pos 0 every theta is 0, cos = 1, sin = 0, and the rotation matrix is I -- for the halves convention and the interleaved one alike, since it is the ANGLE that vanishes and not the pairing. Both columns therefore compute this kernel EXACTLY: the .cpp copies every element, and the .pto multiplies by 1.0, which is exact in IEEE-754 for every finite value. The old note's own reasoning does not bite here -- a STRIDED load is what a FAITHFUL nonzero-pos rope would need, and at pos 0 no rotation is performed at all, so no stride is required. Both emitters now carry a declared-constant pos=0 guard and emit their stub or substitution wording ONLY for a nonzero or dynamic position; neither artefact carries a marker any more (0 occurrences, checked). Device-verified 2026-11-09 against ORACLE 45 (exact identity, ZERO tolerance): 5 of 5 PASS, elements=512 wrong=0 max_abs=0.000e+00, zeros_in_input=0. The claim is EXISTENTIAL -- this shape, this position -- and says nothing about rope at any other position, because at pos 0 a faithful rotation and a plain copy are bit-identical and no device run against this corpus could tell them apart. The refuting class lives in the unit tests: test_tile_rope_emitter (pos=5) and test_pto_rope (pos=42) both still demand the marker, and after this change they are the ONLY thing covering that wording, since no corpus artefact carries it.
rope_v41_8x64.device_ineligible_substitution_2026_11_0: TILE_SUBSTITUTION in its own .cpp: intrinsic=__tile_rope_f32, replacement=identity-copy, reason=missing-cos-sin-operands. Ineligible above `tiled` under the campaign's eligibility gate, and NOT a tolerance or oracle question: the artefact takes TWO GM buffers while rope needs cos and sin, and engine/rope_halves_engine_1x64 -- the faithful one, banked against ORACLE 12 -- takes FOUR. So ORACLE 12 cannot be invoked against this kernel at any arity it has. Recorded 2026-11-08 because the campaign's scorer had never read the marker and both rope rows were still counting toward C_s and L. deepseek_v41's own eligibility_gate note adds the reason the generator cannot simply be fixed here: this shape needs a STRIDED load and __tile_load_f32 takes no stride, which is not true of kimi_k3/rope_k3_1x64, whose generator fix was PROVEN on device 2026-11-07 and never applied to the corpus.

topk_v41_1x384_k6.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED: the arm did not exist and now does. mlir_to_cpp gains __tile_topk_f32. Top-k is k selection passes of ReduceMax plus a scalar first-hit scan, masking each taken position out of a WORKING COPY so the source survives -- it is read twice in the sigmoid variant. The k VALUES leave through the kernel's own store and the k INDICES through the GM pointer the intrinsic takes as its third operand, as int32, the same decision as the argmax index. Was: mlir_to_cpp has no arm for `__tile_topk_f32`. Emitting it would drop the operation silently: the dispatch skips calls it does not match, so the kernel would compile, run, and quietly omit this step.
topk_v41_1x384_k6.device_check: PASS 2026-11-08 on 910B2 (CANN 8.5.2 aarch64, dav-2201), ORACLE 42 (top-k: the k indices, descending by value, ties by LOWER index first), k=6 passed as MV_N, two identical runs: elements=6 wrong=0, want[0..3]=192,96,288,139 got[0..3]=192,96,288,139 EXACT, spread=264 of n=384. The SPREAD is the evidence that this is a selection and not a head extract -- the PTO column's own fallback for this intrinsic is documented as 'a head extract and not a sort', which would have reported spread=5.
topk_v41_1x384_k6.device_check_not_covered: The k VALUES through gm1. This kernel has two outputs and at KERNEL_ARGS == 3 the harness copies back gm2 alone, so the indices are compared and the value store is not. The indices identify the selection completely and the value written is the same one the index was found for, so what is unchecked is whether it reached the right slot of the other buffer. Widening the copy-back would overwrite `b`, which several existing oracles read as an INPUT, so it is not a change an added oracle may make. The oracle PRINTS this line on every run rather than leaving it to be discovered.

embedding_v41_129280x5120.pto_refusal_retracted_2026_11_10: RETRACTED: the op existed and the ARM did not. The old text read -- mlir_to_pto has no arm for `__tile_get_value_f32`. The kernel is a GM row copy and the scalar read-back is the one step this emitter cannot take; the AscendC column carries it. Emitting it anyway would drop the operation silently. -- and its premise, that the scalar read-back is a step this emitter cannot take, was about the emitter and read as if it were about PTO. `ptoas` ships as a Python package, so its op registry is inspectable, and `ptoas/mlir/dialects/_pto_ops_gen.py:22306` has declared `pto.tgetval(src, offset) -> value` all along. It never appears in the corpus's .pto vocabulary because nothing had emitted it -- scraping the corpus for the dialect's ops is a narrowing query, and it returned a plausible absence. mlir_to_pto now has arms for `__tile_get_value_f32` -> `pto.tgetval` and `__tile_load_at_f32` -> a runtime-offset `partition_view`, plus `llvm.mul` on a runtime scalar -> `arith.muli`. Operand and result types were MEASURED, not inferred: of five plausible spellings exactly one assembles (offset `index`, result `f32`). The offset is converted to an integer BEFORE the multiply, so unlike the AscendC path it carries no float-exactness bound on the row width. Inertness: 75 of 75 pre-existing .pto regenerate byte-identically, 0 changed.
embedding_v41_129280x5120.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED 2026-11-08: the bound was real and the LOWERING was wrong. `__tile_embedding_f32` declares its weight table as a tile, so no arm can satisfy it at vocabulary scale -- but the operation does not need that intrinsic. At decode shape it is one row copy from GM: read the index, multiply by the row width, `__tile_load_at_f32` at that element offset. The generator now emits that form and this emitter takes it, with the offset reaching the generated `DataCopy(buf1, gm0Tensor[__v3], ...)` so the table is never resident. Kept rather than deleted so the refusal that licensed `ascendc: null` also records its retirement. Was: UB overflow in kernel 'v41_embedding_5120': __tile_embedding_f32 gathers rows from a tile that holds 5120 element(s) while the vocabulary needs 661913600 (vocab x dim). The table cannot be resident -- it is far larger than the unified buffer -- so its rows have to be copied from global memory one at a time, and mlir_to_cpp has no GM-driven embedding path. Refusing rather than emitting a gather that reads past the tile it was given.

estimated_decode_kernels.source: the published kernel registry's DeepSeek V4 Flash row, read 2026-11-02: 52 distinct kernels, 13 of them traced and 39 read from sources. A floor three times over -- the view is redacted, most rows are unverified by a trace, and V4.1 is a later revision of the same architecture
estimated_decode_kernels.what_it_is: The number of distinct kernels one decode step of this model needs -- the denominator the representation counts are read against. Where the count is KNOWN it is used; where it is not, inventory() derives a LOWER BOUND from the model's own configuration. Not a measurement of a running engine in either case.
estimated_decode_kernels.derivation_error: the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.a_kernel_is: one distinct (operation, shape) pair, because that is what this corpus holds -- one rmsnorm file serves every block that shares D. A layer count does not multiply it.

inventory.line: rmsnorm at D (attn_norm, ffn_norm and the final norm share it)
MLA projections: q_a, q_b, kv_a, kv_b, output
routed expert gate/up at MOE_INTER, and down at D

estimated_decode_kernels.inventory_is_not_used_here: the inventory derives 15 and the known count is 52. The known count wins; the inventory is kept because the gap between them is the measurement of how coarse it is.
uncounted_because_unrecorded: N_SHARED_EXP is not in the registry, so `shared expert gate/up and down` is uncounted
LEADING_DENSE_BLOCKS is not in the registry, so `the leading dense blocks' gate/up at DENSE_FFN_INTER, and down at D` is uncounted

what_the_inventory_collapses.each expert's gate, up and down are one: a real engine has three kernels there, and the gate/up pair is often fused separately from the down-projection
what_the_inventory_collapses.one attention core: decode, prefill and partial/chunked are different kernels with different shapes, and a model with two attention types doubles that again
what_the_inventory_collapses.one matvec per projection: f16 and f32 weight forms are separate kernels, and each quantisation the engine supports adds another (q8_0, q4_K, iq2_xxs, mxfp4 ...)
what_the_inventory_collapses.no prefill shapes: every projection and norm has a batched prefill form, which is a different kernel from its decode form
what_the_inventory_collapses.no quantise/dequantise kernels: activation quantisation and weight unpacking are real kernels; the inventory treats weight format as out of scope
what_the_inventory_collapses.one sampling kernel: argmax is counted; top-p, top-k sampling and draft verification are not

estimated_decode_kernels.why_collapses_are_listed_not_multiplied: 'under-counts by 3.5x' is one number and tells a reader nothing they can act on. These name the specific rows that each stand for several real kernels. They are not multiplied out: that would turn a list of known omissions into a fabricated total. Someone who knows the true count for this model can see which rows to expand.
estimated_decode_kernels.published_registry: the published kernel registry, read 2026-11-02 and generated 2026-08-31, holds 52 distinct kernels for DeepSeek V4 Flash: 13 under a `trace` basis and 39 under `source-scan`. This supersedes an earlier floor of 51; 52 is the larger of the two floors. It stays a floor for three independent reasons -- the published view is marked redacted, so it is a subset; most rows are unverified by a trace, and the registry's own wording is that only a trace is evidence a kernel holds measurable time; and V4.1 is a later revision of the same architecture, so its count can only grow.
